mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger occurs, or the effect reverses in a sample of at least 10 tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 6.5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during a period of wage moderation.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the effect is not statistically significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect disappears during supply-chain normalization.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over a two-month window signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes, or the effect is not robust across at least three historical cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equity sectors and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not significant during periods of high mortgage rates.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between payroll employment (PAYEMS) rising above its 12-month moving average and unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 6% in the same month signals a synchronized labor market tightening, which increases wage growth and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average AND UNRATE < 6% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of such months, or the effect reverses during periods of productivity acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized decline in Real Personal Income (implied from RSAFS and PAYEMS) of more than 1% for three consecutive quarters signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces demand for consumer goods and services and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Implied Real Personal Income annualized decline > -1% for 3 consecutive quarters (from RSAFS and PAYEMS)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered quarters, or the effect is not statistically significant at p < 0.10.
